annotations.text:
Your ad — the landing page half.

Today it is a domain bar and grey strips labelled "plain", "reviews", "a chart", "product shots". Three ways to make it a page you can look at, each with a chart of what the page is worth.

Everything here is a real game: Vella & Co., mid-price performance, writing its own ad, ₹55,000 on the page (reviews) and ₹25,000 on the size guide at round 0.

The pictures are drawn in SVG, not photographs — nothing here claims to be a real product.

The number, checked against the engine rather than assumed.

The page is graded 5 on its own words. landingPageBonus adds 2 points, and liveCapexPaise holds it back until the tranche's liveAtRound — week 4. So the auction uses 5 for weeks 1-3 and 7 from week 4, which is what all three charts draw.

The bonus is applied AFTER grading on purpose (engine/positions.js): two mechanisms writing one number is how the L6 double-count happened.

A gives the page room and reads top to bottom: look at the page, then see what it earned. Costs the most vertical space.

B keeps today's two-column shape, so it is the smallest change and the page stays small.

C is the one that teaches: each part of the page carries what it adds, so the picture and the grade are the same object. CHOSEN by the owner, 2026-09-16.

C first tagged "+1 reviews" and "+1 size chart". That was invented, and checking the engine caught it: landingPageBonus reads the landingPage target ALONE, so the whole +2 comes from the ₹55,000 of reviews and the size guide adds nothing to the grade.

Corrected, C says something the game has never told a player: three purchases, three different mechanisms. The page moves the GRADE; the size guide moves SEND-BACKS (returnRate / sizeGuideEffect); photography moves the CONVERSION RATE (convRateBase × photography). A player who thinks a size guide buys Quality Score is buying the wrong thing.
